data.title: Šurany – a 3D reconstruction of the vanished castle
data.excerpt: We have prepared an idealised reconstruction of Šurany Castle from the period of the Ottoman wars. The castle, which stood at the place known as Podzámeček and was protected by two arms of the Nitra that could be made to flood at will, no longer stands today; its most famous period came with the anti-Ottoman wars and its captain Tomáš Bosniak.

children.text: We have prepared for you an idealised reconstruction of Šurany Castle from the period of the Ottoman wars. Unfortunately the castle no longer stands today.

states of the castle that it stood in what is today Šurany, at the place known as Podzámeček. As late as 1889, when Michal Matunák wrote about this castle, ruins were still visible on its site. Today you would look for them in vain.

The perimeter of the castle was encircled by the river Nitra – by two of its arms. Šurany Castle had the ground plan of a rhomboid. Two main arms and several further arms of the Nitra provided it with reliable protection. The individual arms were flooded as required by means of sluice gates, and the fields and meadows could be flooded as well, which made any siege of the castle more difficult for potential attackers.

Hrady.sk further states that the castle was evidently built in the years 1382 to 1403. In 1403 it is already mentioned as the castle of Voivode Ctibor. In the following years the castle was a centre of rich life. Its most famous period, however, came in the time of the anti-Ottoman wars. An important figure was its owner and captain Tomáš Bosniak. He was born probably in 1580 and died on 19 December 1634, and during his lifetime he became famous as a successful fighter against the Ottomans. The Ottomans probably took Šurany Castle on 10 October 1663 and held it until October 1684. At the end of the 17th and the beginning of the 18th century it was in the hands of Francis II Rákóczi. His uprising of the estates also brought about the demise of the castle. After it was taken by the imperial army on 14 September 1710, no one cared for the damaged castle. The ruins of the castle were left without an owner.

In creating the model we drew on the documentation of RNDr. Miroslav Eliáš (Eliáš, Miroslav. Pamätný spis k dejinám Šurianskeho hradu. – 1st ed. – Šurany: Mestské kultúrne stredisko, 2006) and on his model of the castle, which is kept in the Town Museum in Šurany. Valuable expert advice was also contributed by Ing. Peter Gutek.
